title: Introduce phase markers, NVTX-guarded regions, KV-cache sampler and async trace exporter
author: Katherine Liu
description:
Motivation: We often need low-overhead, deterministic markers across the serving hotpath to correlate scheduler decisions, kernel selection, and KV-cache hits with downstream latency spikes. This PR adds: 1) lightweight phase markers (start/end/annotate) in the runtime that are emitted as both NVTX ranges when NVTX is available and as internal monotonic counters otherwise; 2) NVTX-guarded regions for the hot batching path so external profilers (Nsight / nvprof / perfetto converters) can reliably visualize per-phase GPU work; 3) a continuous KV-cache sampler that periodically records per-request cache hit/miss and approximate key distribution (sampling, not full traces) into a compact ringbuffer; and 4) an asynchronous trace exporter that ships aggregated events (phase counters + sampled K/V metrics) to the perf dashboard backend in a JSONL timeline format. The change is designed to be low-risk: NVTX emission is optional and gated by a runtime flag, the KV sampler uses a bounded ringbuffer and backpressure to avoid affecting latency, and the exporter batches and rate-limits remote writes. Checklist: - [x] implement phase marker API (C++/ABI-stable) - [x] NVTX emission with RAII guard - [x] KV sampler microbench + integration tests - [x] async exporter with retry and rate limit - [x] docs and quickstart for collector configuration - [x] e2e perf dashboard demo and sample traces in docs

Implementation summary: commits are small and focused. phase_markers.cpp/.h provide a scoped PhaseGuard that records start/end timestamps and a small inline annotation payload (string tags limited to 64 bytes). NVTX emission is behind a compile-time weak-link and a runtime flag (env REDWOOD_PROF_NVTX=1) so production builds don't pay the cost unless enabled. The KV sampler (benchmarks/microbench/kv_sampler.cc) hooks into the request completion path with a probabilistic sampler (configurable rate) and writes compact samples into runtime::ProfilerRing (lock-free single-writer ring per-thread). The async trace exporter (tools/perf/trace_sink.go) reads aggregated snapshots via a lightweight RPC endpoint on the control plane and writes newline-delimited JSON events to the perf dashboard ingestion API; exporter backs off on 429s and can spill to local disk when network is degraded.

Files touched (high-level): src/runtime/profiler/phase_markers.cpp, src/runtime/profiler/phase_markers.h, src/runtime/profiler/kv_sampler.cc, tools/perf/trace_sink.go, docs/perf/trace_setup.md, tests/profiler/integration_test.py.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for PhaseGuard serialization and the ringbuffer boundary conditions added under tests/profiler. - Microbench harness added (benchmarks/microbench/kv_sampler.cc) that reports latency delta when sampler enabled vs disabled; results show <0.2% p99 regression at 1% sample rate on our standard 8-GPU host. - End-to-end demo: collected traces from a small continuous-batching workload and imported to the perf dashboard; dashboard annotations correctly correlated KV-cache miss bursts with increased kernel selection time.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind env var and runtime flag; default OFF in hosted builds for first A/B cohort. Deploy to Dedicated can be enabled via config flag. We will monitor two new metrics (profiler.samples_emitted, profiler.export_backoff_seconds) and an alert for elevated export backoffs.

Notes: - This is intentionally conservative: NVTX is optional, and the ringbuffer cannot block the hotpath. - The exporter uses the same ingestion contract as other perf tooling but adds a small version field to allow future schema changes. - Docs include a CLI quickstart for local capture using Nsight and a troubleshooting section for common perf dashboard ingestion errors.

review_comments: Marco Hernandez: Overall looks good. Please make sure NVTX emission is no-op when the weak symbol isn't present; also add a comment about why we limit annotation size to 64 bytes.
Katherine Liu (author): NVTX path is weak-linked and we early-return in the hotpath; added comment and unit test for 64-byte truncation.
Priya Raman: Can we include the sample rate metric as a prometheus counter? We need visibility during rollout.
Katherine Liu: Added profiler.samples_emitted counter and documented it in the rollout plan.
Ethan Cole: Minor nits in Go exporter logging; prefer structured fields for backoff retries.
release_notes: Added a low-overhead PhaseGuard profiler with optional NVTX emission, a sampled KV-cache recorder, and an async trace exporter for perf dashboard ingestion. Feature is opt-in and disabled by default in hosted builds.
qa_notes: Enable REDWOOD_PROF_NVTX=1 and start the local trace_sink with --dashboard-endpoint to reproduce the dashboard import flow. Use benchmarks/microbench/kv_sampler to validate sampler overhead on target hardware.
